messages:
maria (eng-security): quick alert 1: restore job for tenant-871 surfaced an unencrypted snapshot in object store while performing a test restore. not clear if snapshot was created that way or if encryption step was skipped on upload.
jon (eng-sre): which bucket/key? any chance it was a staging artifact?
maria (eng-security): key=backups/tenant-871/snapshots/2026-04-10/snap-871-4e2a.tmp.enc? actually the object header shows Content-Encoding: identity and x-amz-server-side-encryption missing. full key: backups/tenant-871/snapshots/2026-04-10/snap-871-4e2a
tanya (eng-platform): hmm odd name. our naming usually ends with .enc when agent encrypts client-side. missing SSE header suggests client didn't request SSE-KMS.
oliver (backup-agent): that key looks like an old agent v1 behavior in fallback mode. if local encryption fails and retry path uploads to bucket to preserve data, we tag with .tmp normally. but this one lost suffix. i'll check agent logs for that host.
jon (eng-sre): pulled S3 metadata: ETag=6f1a2b3c4d, x-amz-meta-agent-version=1.8.0, x-amz-meta-uploader=backup-node-07, server-side-encryption: none. requestId: 9F5ABXWJQ9H4R.
maria (eng-security): we need containment: copy object to forensics bucket, grant read-only to sec team, then delete original. also require an audit entry with ETag+requestId.
tanya (eng-platform): before deletion we should snapshot Object Lock and record CloudTrail with PutObject event. I'll run aws s3api head-object and copy to s3://redwood-forensics/snapshots/3976543210/ then lifecycle-delete original.
oliver (backup-agent): found logs on backup-node-07: '2026-04-10T22:40:01Z ERROR encrypt: failed to open /var/tmp/enc-keyring: permission denied', then '2026-04-10T22:40:03Z WARN fallback: uploading unencrypted to preserve copy', then PutObject to key backups/tenant-871/snapshots/2026-04-10/snap-871-4e2a.
maria (eng-security): that permission denied is new. whose file is that keyring? KMS data key cache lives on node and is owned by backup-agent:backup. perhaps a packaging change changed permissions.
jon (eng-sre): checking package diff from last deployment: indeed a postinstall script changed umask for the agent to 0022 which made the keyring unreadable to agent runtime which runs as backup-agent user.
tanya (eng-platform): so we have a deployment-induced regression. immediate steps: 1) replace obj with forensics copy, 2) rotate uploader creds for that node, 3) revoke agent image/tag 1.8.0 from auto-deploy, 4) push rollback to previous image for fleet.
sec-bot: creating incident INC-2026-0511 and assigning to eng-security + eng-sre.
maria (eng-security): we also need to tighten RBAC: backup-agent node role should not be permitted to PutObject without s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption = aws:kms. add explicit deny for non-kms on the bucket.
tanya (eng-platform): we can add a policy statement with Deny when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption != aws:kms for resources arn:aws:s3:::redwood-backups-prod/backups/* and ensure CI enforces the policy for new roles.
oliver (backup-agent): agent code will be updated to fail fast if local encryption fails instead of fallback upload. also adding a start-time preflight that verifies keyring accessible and that GenerateDataKey succeeds. I'll open PR with tests.
jon (eng-sre): forensics copy done, original object deleted, creds rotated for backup-node-07, rollback initiated. monitoring for similar keys across last 30 days with pattern '/snapshots/*' and missing SSE.
maria (eng-security): detection: add CloudTrail filter and sigma rule: eventName=PutObject AND requestParameters.bucketName=redwood-backups-prod AND NOT requestParameters.headers.x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms -> alert. also add detector for PutObject from agent-version 1.8.0 without SSE.
tanya (eng-platform): also audit KMS key policy: require EncryptionContext with key 'purpose=backup' for GenerateDataKey calls. add Reject if missing. tests in KMS staging should exercise encryption-context mismatch.
jon (eng-sre): quick vuln triage: severity high for that tenant because unencrypted snapshot existed in S3 for unknown window; we need to notify legal/privacy if any customer data exposed. engaging Legal.
maria (eng-security): notify affected tenant (tenant-871) via CS per template; include remediation timeline and whether keys rotated.
oliver (backup-agent): patch note: disallow fallback upload by default; env var ALLOW_UNENCRYPTED_FALLBACK=false to enable in emergency. adding integration test to CI that uploads to a fake S3 and asserts header x-amz-server-side-encryption=aws:kms.
jon (eng-sre): rolling scan found 4 other keys in last 14 days with missing SSE, all uploaded by 1.8.0 canaries. copying to forensics and deleting originals. creating a short lived runbook for manual review of their content.
tanya (eng-platform): change deployed: IAM deny for non-kms PutObject applied to bucket, policy applied to node role. CMK policy updated to require encryption context 'purpose:backup'.
maria (eng-security): postmortem scheduled tomorrow 10am PT. action items recap in runbook: update packaging to preserve keyring perms, fail-fast agent patch, CI tests, IAM deny rule, CloudTrail detectors, tenant notification, rotate creds.
sec-bot: postmortem ticket PM-2026-0511 created and linked to INC-2026-0511.
maria (eng-security): thanks all. keep monitoring channel and post any new findings here. :eyes:
